summary.text: Mary Gay Scanlon is the Democratic incumbent for Pennsylvania's 5th District, in the U.S. House since a November 2018 special election. A lawyer who worked in legal-aid and child-advocacy roles and later directed pro bono programs at a national law firm, she also served as president of her local school board. She serves on the Judiciary and Rules committees.

paragraphs.text: Scanlon was born in Syracuse, New York, in 1959.
She earned a bachelor's degree in history from Colgate University in 1980 and a J.D. from the University of Pennsylvania Law School in 1984.
She worked as a law clerk and as an attorney at Ballard Spahr, the Education Law Center of Pennsylvania and the Support Center for Child Advocates.

Her official biography says Scanlon was national pro bono counsel at a major U.S. law firm, where she directed and supervised more than 600 lawyers in 15 offices providing more than 50,000 hours of pro bono legal services annually.
Before Congress she served as president of her local school board and as co-chair of the Voting Rights Task Force of the Association of Pro Bono Counsel.
She was sworn into the U.S. House on November 13, 2018, following a special election.

Scanlon serves on the House Committee on Rules and the Judiciary Committee, where she is ranking member of the Constitution and Limited Government Subcommittee, and she chairs the House Caucuses on Access to Legal Aid, Youth Mentoring, and Foster Youth.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), Ballotpedia lists her Judiciary subcommittees as Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement and The Constitution and Limited Government, and her Rules subcommittee as Rules and Organization of the House.
According to her official biography, she lives in Swarthmore with her husband, Mark, and they have three adult children.
